tolerance_policy.rationale: Reference values are recorded at full float precision in reproducibility/canonical-run.json. 1e-9 is the study's own canonical-run verification tolerance (scripts/canonical_run.py METRIC_TOLERANCE), more than seven orders of magnitude below the 0.05 degF practical-tie tolerance, so no difference inside it can change a scientific decision. Identities, hashes, counts, periods, parameters and decisions are compared exactly; only floating-point quantities use the numeric tolerance.

evidence_gaps.description: canonical-run.json pins the backtesting parameters but not the per-fold schedule or the fold-local seasonal scales; the contract derives the schedule from the pinned parameters, enforces it as a gate, and the report records the reproduced fold scales without a reference.
Fold-level metrics, horizon-wise MAE and out-of-sample forecast rows are not versioned by the study; the reproduction reports them (backtest-forecasts.json) without an expected side.

canonical-run.json records the complete specification only for the selected candidate; the fixed parameters of the other nine are pinned through scripts/forecasting_model_selection.py (file_text locators).
The study records failure counts and failure kinds per specification, not which folds failed or why; the reproduction reports its own per-fold failure categories.

holdout_exposure.description: Notebook 01 explored the complete 1920-01..1939-12 series retrospectively (including STL strengths and CUSUM stability with a trend + calendar-month design) before the 1939 holdout was prospectively sealed from Notebook 02 onward, and those full-series diagnostics informed the design of the frozen catalog. The holdout was never used to score, tune or select, the model was frozen before the single final evaluation, and it was evaluated once -- but it is not an exploration-blind external test set in the strongest sense (study review REV-001).
holdout_exposure.provenance: scientific_study_run (inherited study fact, verified against the pinned canonical run; not something a reproduction can re-establish)
holdout_exposure.reproduction_consequence: the reproduction evaluates the same holdout once and never uses it for selection or adjustment, but it inherits the study's exploration visibility: the holdout is not an exploration-blind external test set

limitations: Educational univariate study of one short monthly series (240 observations); no operational or climate claim.
The 1939 holdout is procedurally sealed but not exploration-blind (REV-001).
Twelve holdout points give an imprecise final-evaluation estimate; the backtest (108 forecasts per specification) carries the selection evidence.
Numerical optimizers (Holt-Winters, SARIMAX) may differ in their last digits across CPU architectures; agreement is established within the declared tolerance, not byte identity.

study_observations.description: The canonical run executed on Linux-aarch64 with CPython 3.13.13 and the locked packages; a reproduction on another architecture or interpreter patch is at best 'compatible'.

The study reports failures by exception class name. Its own guard exception (ForecastingModelSelectionError) covers explicit optimizer non-convergence and invalid forecast output; Atlas records those as guard categories and reports them in the study vocabulary through failure_policy.study_guard_failure_kind. Any other exception keeps its type name.
The study's joblib artifact and model_state_fingerprint describe its own serialized model; a reproduction never loads or re-creates them, so byte-identical model state is not claimed.
canonical-run.json keeps a superseded, unlocked execution (statsmodels 0.14.6, AutoReg old_names keyword) as provenance only; it is not a reproduction target.

superseded_reference.summary: A previous unlocked execution (Python 3.12.13, statsmodels 0.14.6) whose catalog still used the AutoReg old_names keyword; a clean statsmodels 0.15 install silently made both AutoReg candidates ineligible. Kept by the study as traceable provenance; the reproduction targets only the current locked canonical run.

backtesting.fold_schedule_provenance: Derived deterministically from the pinned backtesting parameters (development start, initial training, origin step, horizon, fold count); the canonical run does not version the per-fold schedule. Enforced as a protocol gate and corroborated by the README (validation years 1930 -> 1938).
